Walter Pitts fue un autodidacta que nunc: Walter Pitts was a self-taught man who never obtained a university degree; at twelve he was already arguing by letter with Bertrand Russell. In 1969, Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published Perceptrons, a book that rigorously proved the limits of a single layer, starting with XOR. It contributed to a fall in interest and funding for neural networks lasting more than a decade. They came back strongly in 1986, when David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton and Ronald Williams popularised backpropagation, the method for sharing out the blame among layers, which is no more than the [[fn-derivadas|chain rule]] applied many times.
